newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland role limited in U.S. arms plan for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Poland role limited in U.S. arms plan for Bosnia.

text.p: Poland told a special U.S. envoy on Friday that it would offer only limited help in arming Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation, partly because of European Union reservations over the Washington-sponsored scheme.

"We treat the Train and Equip programme as the next step towards restoring stability in the Balkans," Deputy Foreign Minister Robert Mroziewicz said after talks in Warsaw with U.S. Balkan envoy James Pardew.
"We would like to stress however, that we would like to participate in it at the lowest possible level," Mroziewicz told a news conference.
Pardew came to Warsaw to find out what Poland would do to help the programme, which aims to ensure Moslem-Croat forces can defend themselves against aggression.

He said after meeting Polish industry, foreign and defence ministries officials, as well as the General Staff and the National Security Office, that Poland had yet to decide the scope of its participation and more meetings would follow.
"The Polish government... it has to decide at which level it wants to participate," Pardew told reporters.
"There is a range of activities in which Poland could take part from non-lethal training to equipment," Pardew said.
Mroziewicz said Poland would decide the extent of its involvement only after Bosnia's elections on September 14.
Poland was interested in selling mainly defensive systems rather than offensive weapons, officials said.

In August Polish newspapers reported that the United States had asked Poland to provide up to 45 T-72 tanks, worth some $50 million, to be paid for out of a NATO fund. The prospect was eagerly welcomed by the country's struggling arms industry.
But Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati said during a trip to the United States that Poland would not sell tanks in line with the European Union's arms embargo to the region.
Pardew said the U.S. would press EU states to lift the ban.
"We think it is critical that European governments stand with the United States in helping Bosnia create a military force for self-defence," he said.
Pardew said the issue of Polish tank sales was not taken further on Friday.
"The tank issue has been resolved -- the U.S. will provide 45 M60A3 tanks to Bosnia probably in Mid-October," he said. "That is not to say that in the future we do not want to discuss tanks."
